## Behavior

At exact HEAD `6bea169553919a03cad0eb375e4189240ad9ddf4`, replace `promoteStageAtomically`’s visible `mkdir(dest)` plus per-entry moves. Build and validate the complete docket only in the ignored archive-local stage, complete required raw-scratch deletion, then publish the stage tree at the final name in one same-filesystem, kernel-atomic **no-replace** operation. Before that operation the final identity is absent; afterward it is the complete staged tree. A collision loses without altering either winner or pre-existing destination; a publication failure returns Recorder status 125 and leaves no partial final identity. Preserve symlink rejection, exact child exit/signal on Recorder success, Recorder precedence and exact child outcome on Recorder failure, ignored staging, and the absence of production fault hooks.

## Owner

The publication invariant belongs at the Recorder filesystem-promotion seam in `src/recorder/run.ts` (with a small dedicated helper only if needed to encapsulate the platform no-replace primitive). `src/recorder/paths.ts` continues to own ignored-stage allocation, containment, and same-filesystem proof. Do not represent atomicity by manifest-last convention: the prior commit `472a05e` already tried that method family, and current code exposes a claimed final directory while moving entries one by one.

## Red

Add focused black-box counterexamples to `test/recorder-transaction.test.ts` (and only minimal harness support in `test/helpers/recorder-test-harness.ts`):

1. **Observer/publication counterexample:** repeatedly observe the final pathname while a docket with multiple artifacts is published; every observation must be either absent or a complete core (manifest plus every manifest-referenced stored artifact), never an empty/partial final directory.
2. **Crash-residue counterexample:** terminate the Recorder during the pre-publication window and prove the final pathname is absent; only private ignored stage residue may remain. Dispose the temporary crash probe by graduating this behavior exactly once into this transaction suite.
3. **Race/no-overwrite counterexample:** synchronize two recorders at publication for one identity, including the empty-directory overwrite case that plain directory `rename` permits; assert exactly one complete winner, loser status 125/`destination-exists`, no mixed tree, and no overwrite/removal of a pre-existing file, directory, or symlink.

First demonstrate these fail against HEAD’s `mkdir(dest)`/entry-loop implementation.

## Green

Implement a true create-if-absent atomic tree publication primitive—never a check-then-rename emulation and never destination reservation followed by entry materialization. Revalidate containment and parent identity immediately before publication, prove stage and destination parent share a device, map the primitive’s occupied-name result to `destination-exists`, and map other failures to `promotion-failed`. On success, ownership of the whole stage transfers in the single operation; on failure, clean only the private stage and never delete or mutate the contested final name. Keep required raw cleanup before this call. Regenerate the tracked Recorder build output with `npm run build:recorder`.

Verify with:

- focused red/green transaction tests;
- `npm run typecheck`;
- `npm test`;
- `npm run build:recorder` followed by package/lifecycle coverage to ensure the shipped `dist`/bin path has identical behavior.

## Scope

Authorized files are limited to the Recorder publication implementation (`src/recorder/run.ts`, `src/recorder/paths.ts` only if its ownership requires adjustment, and any minimal dedicated no-replace helper), corresponding tracked `dist/recorder/*`, `test/recorder-transaction.test.ts`, and minimal recorder test-harness/package-lifecycle changes needed to exercise the real production seam. No README, Soul, schema, role-runtime, packet, session, or unrelated cleanup work; no production test hooks. Apply as one coherent forward commit from this HEAD, with the repository’s existing `fix(recorder): …` prefix, and report the new commit SHA plus exact dispositions for observer, crash residue, race/no-overwrite, symlink safety, raw cleanup, status 125, and child-outcome preservation.
